context: Group 1 needs a decision before code: does BenchBox claim Windows support for the MCP durable-job surface? pyproject declares no Operating System classifier and the README references Windows only for installation. If yes, debug the job lifecycle on Windows -- the ExceptionGroup at jobs.py:771 is the entry point. If no, scope those tests to POSIX with the reason recorded, the way PR #1853 did for the make-target tests. Group 2 needs a Windows box or a self-hosted runner; until then leave both failing rather than skipping blind.
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-24 from nightly run 32684255652 (workflow_dispatch on develop). 18 of 24 jobs pass. PR #1858 addresses two of the six failures (ubuntu-3.10 tomllib, scheduled-workflow-liveness). These three remain, all Windows:

  test (windows-latest, 3.10)
  test (windows-latest, 3.12)
  integration-smoke (windows-latest, 3.12)

GROUP 1 -- MCP durable jobs, the only genuinely product-facing part. Seven tests across tests/integration/mcp/test_durable_jobs.py, tests/integration/mcp/test_multiworker_acceptance.py and tests/unit/mcp/test_durable_jobs.py. Jobs never reach 'completed': assertions read 'queued' == 'completed' or 'failed' == 'completed', with an ExceptionGroup at benchbox/mcp/jobs.py:771. One test additionally hits MCPError(-32004, 'Request rate limit exceeded'). This is shipped-product behaviour on a platform the README documents for install, so it needs a decision, not a skip.

GROUP 2 -- two failures I deliberately did NOT touch in PR #1853 because they are not honestly diagnosable from a log without a Windows machine:
  tests/unit/scripts/test_check_makefile_inventory.py::test_semantic_assignment_reorder_fails_and_changes_gnu_make_evaluation -- AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'splitlines'. subprocess.run there uses capture_output=True and text=True, which should guarantee a str, so the cause is not visible from the message alone.
  tests/unit/scripts/test_check_release_curation.py::test_curated_release_removes_dangling_project_test_and_runs_retained_tests -- a PytestBenchmarkWarning about xdist surfacing as a failure.

Guessing at either from a log line is how a skip lands on a test that would have passed, which is the mistake PR #1853 was written to avoid.

Blocks nightly-red-blocks-release-evidence w4 (consecutive green runs), which blocks w5 (the committed UAT evidence release-guide.md requires for v0.4.0).

verifications.expected: test (windows-latest, 3.10 and 3.12) and integration-smoke (windows-latest, 3.12) all green
